request: Explain current Markdown interpreter/render libraries and investigate more efficient alternatives.

current.parser: Vendored swiftlang/swift-cmark0.9.0/cmark-gfm at08ddb528923cc1a6527e02b7a1aee9e516ca749a, with recorded local configuration/metadata-extension bridges and CommonMark0.31.2 backports. This is not an unmodified upstream dependency.
current.integration: MarkdownProcessor Swift actor owns one native parse and supplies HTML plus an owned Swift AST/source metadata. Custom Swift dialect extensions preserve features. It currently reparses the whole document.
current.html: cmark_render_html plus Swift feature decoration, shared styles/templates and resource handling.
current.display: Apple WKWebView; persistent shell and DOM update integration. Source editing is native TextKit2.
current.verifiedCore: 354 package tests/76 suites;652 CommonMark examples;8 arm64 executables in downloaded12a356c core artifacts.

candidates.name: swiftlang/swift-markdown
candidates.finding: Current README still identifies cmark-gfm as parsing engine. A Swift interface does not by itself establish a speed gain; earlier0.9 evaluation had renderer/footnote/escaping integration gaps.

candidates.name: MD4C
candidates.finding: Callback parser avoids building its own large document tree; CommonMark/GFM extensions and HTML renderer. First candidate for an apples-to-apples efficiency comparison, without assuming advertised speed applies to Snowfolio AST/source ranges/extensions.

candidates.name: pulldown-cmark
candidates.finding: Rust pull parser, source maps and HTML output; low-allocation design. Requires another toolchain and Swift boundary; benchmark benefit and full dialect/source-coordinate parity before considering migration.

candidates.name: Textual
candidates.finding: Native SwiftUI rendering with Foundation Markdown and pluggable parsers; selection/math/styling. Interesting native display candidate, not a verified replacement for existing HTML/CSS/template/export/diagram behavior.

decision: Keep cmark-gfm for production. MD4C has faster/lower-memory bare parsing but fails59 of184 existing optional-dialect output expectations using its upstream flags. Full AST/source-position/editor/preview parity is also unproven. Adopt the measured Swift parent-tracking optimization without changing grammar or output.
evaluationGate: Representative100KB/1MB/10MB and pathological fixtures; releasearm64 on same host.
Measure parse-only and complete source metadata/AST/HTML generation separately from WebKit publication, typing and scroll performance.
Measure cold/warm time, peak/resident growth and allocations.
Require652CommonMark examples, feature corpus, UTF8/UTF16 source mapping, unsafe-input boundaries, extensions, custom styles/templates and export parity.
Prefer fewer native-engine patches and integration code only when behavior and measured results support the replacement.
benchmarkStatus: Completed matched arm64 -Os cmark/MD4C core comparison, optional dialect fixtures, full-pipeline baseline/optimization, and paired five-process confirmation. Detailed evidence in markdown-engine-comparison.json.
